Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh
Bench: Sanjay Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 9547 of 2022
Applicant :- Pintu
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Pankaj Kumar Tiwari,Krishna Kumar Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajeet Kumar Srivastava Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and Mr. Ajeet Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the first informant/complainant.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant- Pintu, who is involved in Case Crime No. 503 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366A, 376(3) I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Sahaswan, District- Buduan, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case in brief, informant who is father of the victim, lodged an F.I.R. on 21.11.2021 against the applicant with the allegation inter-alia that his daughter has been missing since 18.11.2021 (at about 7 pm), the hectic search was made to trace the victim then it was revealed that she has been enticed away by the present applicant Pintu.
When he went to the house of the applicant, his house was locked and other family members of the applicant had absconded.

sentences.text: It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that victim was major and she was consenting party with the applicant.

In support of this submission, it is pointed out that victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has disclosed her age about 18 years, but when she produced for her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the learned Magistrate, she has stated that she is aged about 13 years.
F.I.R. has been lodged after a delay of three days.
Therefore, the applicant who is languishing in jail since 15.12.2021 is entitled for bail.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that as per ossification test report dated 18.12.2021 of the victim, her radiological age is about 16 years.

It is also pointed out that as per Transfer Certificate of Class VIIth of the victim, her date of birth is 07.07.2009 and according to which also the victim is minor, which is also the part of the case diary.
It is also submitted that victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has made serious allegation of rape against the applicant.
Therefore, considering the gravity of offence, the bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that as per ossification test report of the victim, her elbow was fused, her knee was partially fused whereas her wrist and clavical were not fused.
Hence, the opinion of the Doctor that victim is aged about 16 years, is liable to be accepted.
So far as delay of three days in lodging F.I.R. is concerned
, it is well settled that in the sexual offences cases, the delay in lodging F.I.R. is immaterial.

Considering the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim, I find that she, in her statement has given vivid description of the incident, making allegation inter-alia of rape on her by the applicant.

Vide order dated 25.01.2023, the present status of the trial of the applicant was called for, pursuant to which,
the trial Court is submitted its report dated 03.02.2023, which is on record mentioning therein that on 14.11.2022, victim appeared before the trial Court and her examination-in-chief was recorded but from the side of applicant- Pintu, his counsel did not appear for cross-examination, therefore,
opportunity of cross-examination was closed.
In the report, it is also mentioned that the trial will be completed expeditiously, fixing short dates in the matter.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the submissions advanced on behalf of parties, gravity of offence, role assigned to applicant, severity of punishment and report of the trial Court, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected at this stage.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
